_comment: One sentence per org, keyed by slug, shown under the org page header. `bun run seed` writes it to orgs.description and clears the column for any org not listed here, so this file owns it.

descriptions.1day-sooner: Advocacy nonprofit representing volunteers in human challenge trials and other intensive infectious-disease studies, and pushing for faster vaccine development.
descriptions.80-000-hours: Career advice organization that produces research, a podcast and one-on-one advising to steer people into high-impact work, with AI safety as its top-rated problem.
descriptions.affine: Runs the AFFINE Seminar, a month-long residency for agent-foundations and alignment-theory research led by Johannes Mayer.
descriptions.ai-futures-project: Nonprofit research group forecasting the trajectory of advanced AI, best known for the AI 2027 scenario and the AI Futures Model, with related policy engagement.
descriptions.ai-lab-watch: Zach Stein-Perlman's one-person project collecting and scoring the safety practices of frontier AI companies; no longer maintained since September 2025.
descriptions.ai-policy-institute: Research organization, AIPI, best known for polling American public opinion on AI, alongside lobbying and crisis-response preparation.
descriptions.ai-risk-mitigation-fund: Grantmaking fund spun out of the Long-Term Future Fund, housed at Effective Ventures, making grants to projects reducing catastrophic risk from transformative AI.
descriptions.ai-safety-and-governance-fund: Volunteer-run fund that tests which AI-risk messages persuade the public and spreads the ones that work.
descriptions.ai-safety-camp: Online program that teams up aspiring AI safety researchers to work on concrete projects under a research lead for several months.
descriptions.ai-safety-info: Rob Miles's project explaining AI existential risk to a general audience through YouTube videos and the aisafety.info FAQ.
descriptions.ai-safety-south-africa: AI safety research and community-building organization in Cape Town, founded as AI Safety Cape Town and now the Cape Institute for Safe AI.
descriptions.ai-standards-lab: Independent nonprofit that accelerates the drafting of AI safety standards by contributing technical work to standards bodies.
descriptions.aistof: Pooled multi-donor fund run by JueYan Zhang that makes fast grants on emerging AI safety opportunities in governance, technical alignment and evaluations.
descriptions.alignment-of-complex-systems-research-gr: Prague research group, ACS, at Charles University studying alignment in multi-agent systems of humans and AIs, including hierarchical agents.
descriptions.alignment-research-center: Research nonprofit, ARC, founded by Paul Christiano, pursuing theoretically motivated approaches to aligning machine learning systems.
descriptions.alliance-to-feed-the-earth-in-disasters: Research nonprofit, ALLFED, working on resilient food sources to feed everyone after a nuclear winter or other global catastrophe.
descriptions.alter-israel: Israeli research and advocacy organization, the Association for Long Term Existence and Resilience, working on AI safety and biosecurity policy in Israel.
descriptions.americans-for-responsible-innovation: Washington advocacy nonprofit, ARI, lobbying for public-interest policy on AI and other emerging technologies.
descriptions.apart-research: AI safety nonprofit running research hackathons and a lab program that turns hackathon projects into published research.
descriptions.apollo-research: London AI safety lab that evaluates frontier models for scheming and deception and advises governments and labs on model evaluations and governance.
descriptions.arcadia-impact: UK charity running field-building programs for AI safety, including student groups and training for people moving into the field.
descriptions.atlas-computing: Nonprofit that mapped and launched missing AI-risk organizations, since reorganized as Atlas Ignota under Convergent Research.
descriptions.atlas-fellowship: Scholarship and summer program for talented high-school students, run from 2022 until it wound down in late 2023.
descriptions.balsa-policy-institute: Zvi Mowshowitz's policy research organization, Balsa Research, building the evidence base for reforms such as repeal of the Jones Act.
descriptions.beri: Berkeley nonprofit that supports university existential-risk research groups such as CHAI with staff, funding and operations.
descriptions.bipartisan-commission-on-biodefense: Privately funded commission of former US officials that assesses US biodefense and issues recommendations, now hosted at the Atlantic Council.
descriptions.bluedot-impact: Runs the AI Safety Fundamentals courses and related training programs that bring people into AI safety work, and makes small grants to alumni projects.
descriptions.blueprint-biosecurity: Research and advocacy nonprofit working to make the world ready for the next pandemic, with a focus on next-generation PPE and far-UVC germicidal light.
descriptions.campaign-for-ai-safety: Public-awareness and advocacy campaign for laws restricting dangerous AI development, merged into the Existential Risk Observatory in 2024.
descriptions.carboncopies-foundation-for-substrate-in: Volunteer-run nonprofit pursuing research toward whole brain emulation.
descriptions.catalyze-impact: Incubator for new organizations in AI safety, security and resilience.
descriptions.center-for-a-new-american-security: Washington national-security think tank, CNAS, whose technology and national security program covers AI policy.
descriptions.center-for-ai-policy: Nonpartisan advocacy organization, CAIP, that lobbied for US legislation on catastrophic AI risk before ceasing most operations in 2025 for lack of funding.
descriptions.center-for-ai-safety: San Francisco AI safety nonprofit that does technical research, runs a shared compute cluster and fellowships, and organized the 2023 Statement on AI Risk.
descriptions.center-for-applied-rationality: Berkeley nonprofit, CFAR, that teaches applied rationality through workshops.
descriptions.center-for-human-compatible-ai: UC Berkeley research center founded by Stuart Russell to reorient AI toward provably beneficial systems, training PhD students and postdocs in alignment.
descriptions.center-for-security-and-emerging-technol: Georgetown University policy research center that analyzes the security implications of AI and other emerging technologies for US policymakers.
descriptions.centre-for-effective-altruism: Builds and supports the effective altruism community through EA Global conferences, the EA Forum, local groups and community health work.
descriptions.centre-for-enabling-ea-learning-research: Residential centre in Blackpool, CEEALAR, offering free accommodation to people working on EA and AI safety projects.
descriptions.centre-for-long-term-resilience: UK think tank, CLTR, working on policy for extreme risks from AI and biological threats.
descriptions.centre-for-the-governance-of-ai: Oxford-based research nonprofit studying how to govern advanced AI, producing policy research and training researchers through its fellowship programs.
descriptions.cesia: Paris nonprofit, the Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA, doing AI safety policy research, public awareness work and talent development in France.
descriptions.charter-cities-institute: Nonprofit promoting new cities with better governance as a route out of poverty.
descriptions.civic-ai-security-program: Nonprofit, known as CivAI, that builds live software demonstrations of AI capabilities and risks and briefs policymakers, civil society and the public with them.
descriptions.civitech-incubator: Program within the voter-engagement company Civitech to recruit and fund founders, operators and researchers to launch new civic-engagement projects for US democracy.
descriptions.coefficient-giving: Largest philanthropic funder of AI safety work, formerly Open Philanthropy, making grants across global health, animal welfare and global catastrophic risks.
descriptions.computational-rational-agents-laboratory: Research group, CORAL, studying agent foundations to develop mathematical tools for aligning AI objectives with human values.
descriptions.constellation: Berkeley research center hosting AI safety researchers and organizations in a shared workspace, with visiting-fellow and residency programs.
descriptions.controlai: Advocacy nonprofit campaigning for government action to prevent extinction risk from superintelligent AI.
descriptions.convergence-analysis: Research organization producing AI scenario analysis and governance recommendations.
descriptions.convergent-research: Launches focused research organizations, FROs, to build scientific capabilities that fall between academia and startups.
descriptions.cooperative-ai-foundation: UK charity, CAIF, funding research to improve the cooperative capabilities of advanced AI.
descriptions.council-on-strategic-risks: Washington security policy institute, CSR, working on nuclear, climate, biological and other systemic risks.
descriptions.ea-funds: Grantmaking platform run by the Centre for Effective Altruism that pools donations into expert-managed funds, including the Transformative AI Fund.
descriptions.effective-institutions-project: Research and advisory organization that helps donors improve the decision-making of the world's most important institutions, including on AI governance.
descriptions.effective-ventures-foundation: Umbrella charity, in UK and US entities, that has fiscally sponsored the Centre for Effective Altruism, 80,000 Hours, Giving What We Can and other EA projects.
descriptions.emergent-ventures: Tyler Cowen's fellowship and small-grant program at the Mercatus Center for individuals with ambitious ideas.
descriptions.encode: Youth-led advocacy organization lobbying for AI safety legislation in the United States, including California's SB 1047 and SB 53.
descriptions.epistea-z-s: Prague umbrella organization running existential-security residencies, workshops and a coworking space, and fiscally sponsoring projects such as ACS and PIBBSS.
descriptions.epoch-ai: Research institute that collects data on AI models, compute and training runs and publishes trend analysis and benchmarks on the trajectory of AI.
descriptions.existential-risk-laboratory: University of Chicago lab, known as XLab, that runs a summer research fellowship and coursework on existential risks from nuclear weapons, AI and other threats.
descriptions.existential-risk-observatory: Dutch nonprofit working to reduce existential risk by informing public debate, including research on pausing AI development.
descriptions.far-ai: AI safety research nonprofit, FAR.AI, that does alignment and robustness research, runs an incubator for new research agendas, and hosts the FAR Labs coworking space.
descriptions.fli: Nonprofit, the Future of Life Institute, that funds and advocates for reducing large-scale risks from AI and other transformative technologies.
descriptions.focal-at-cmu: Foundations of Cooperative AI Lab at Carnegie Mellon University, led by Vincent Conitzer, studying game theory for cooperation among AI agents.
descriptions.forecasting-research-institute: Research nonprofit developing forecasting methods for high-stakes decisions, including the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament.
descriptions.foresight-institute: Research organization founded in 1986 that runs fellowships, grants and events on nanotechnology, longevity, neurotechnology and safe AI.
descriptions.foundation-for-american-innovation: Technology policy think tank, FAI, doing research, fellowships and outreach to government.
descriptions.future-of-humanity-institute: University of Oxford research institute founded by Nick Bostrom that studied existential risk and the long-term future, closed in April 2024.
descriptions.future-of-life-foundation: Foundation affiliated with the Future of Life Institute that incubates projects to empower humanity in the age of AI.
descriptions.geodesic-research: UK technical AI safety organization doing compute-intensive alignment research, hosted by Meridian Impact.
descriptions.global-priorities-institute: University of Oxford research institute that studied global priorities in philosophy and economics from 2018 until closing in July 2025.
descriptions.good-ancestor-foundation: Austin, Texas foundation funding tools to make civilization more robust to catastrophes.
descriptions.good-impressions: Marketing agency doing outreach for socially impactful projects, including AI safety organizations.
descriptions.hadrian-biodefense: Organization building capacity for civilization to withstand and recover from severe biological crises.
descriptions.horizon-institute-for-public-service: Runs fellowships placing technologists in US government and policy institutions to work on AI and biosecurity.
descriptions.ilina-program: African-led organization advancing AI safety through research, policy engagement and talent development.
descriptions.impact-academy: Talent accelerator, renamed SteadRise, that trains people and helps them transition into technical AI safety work.
descriptions.improve-the-news-foundation: Nonprofit founded by Max Tegmark that runs Verity, a news aggregator designed to show bias and present multiple perspectives.
descriptions.institute-for-ai-policy-and-strategy: Think tank, IAPS, that produces policy research on frontier AI for governments, covering compute governance, international security and lab oversight.
descriptions.institute-for-law-ai: Independent think tank, LawAI, formerly the Center for Law and AI Risk, researching and advising on the legal challenges of advanced AI.
descriptions.institute-for-progress: Washington think tank, IFP, working on innovation policy, including metascience, immigration, biosecurity and AI.
descriptions.intelligence-rising: Runs the Intelligence Rising roleplay workshop in which decision-makers experience the dynamics of competitive AI development.
descriptions.international-association-for-safe-and-e: Membership association, IASEAI, convening researchers and policymakers on safe and ethical AI through conferences, standards and policy work.
descriptions.johns-hopkins-center-for-health-security: Research center at Johns Hopkins University studying how to prevent and respond to epidemics, pandemics and other biological threats.
descriptions.kairos: Runs field-building programs for AI safety, including the SPAR mentored research program and the FSP fellowship for university students.
descriptions.langsikt-centre-for-long-term-policy: Norwegian think tank for long-term policy, including AI governance.
descriptions.lawzero: Nonprofit founded by Yoshua Bengio developing safe-by-design AI systems, starting with Scientist AI.
descriptions.legal-advocates-for-safe-science-and-tec: Legal nonprofit, LASST, that brings lawsuits on catastrophic risk and defends whistleblowers in science and technology.
descriptions.lightcone-foundation: Nevada private foundation whose stated purpose is supporting the Future of Life Foundation; unrelated to Lightcone Infrastructure.
descriptions.lightcone-infrastructure: Runs LessWrong, the AI Alignment Forum and the Lighthaven campus in Berkeley, infrastructure for the rationality and AI safety communities.
descriptions.longview-philanthropy: Philanthropic advisory firm that helps major donors give to reduce existential risk, and runs pooled funds on emerging challenges and nuclear weapons policy.
descriptions.ltff: EA Funds' Long-Term Future Fund, which made grants mostly to individuals working on AI existential risk until it was replaced by the Transformative AI Fund.
descriptions.machine-intelligence-research-institute: Berkeley nonprofit, MIRI, founded in 2000 to study AI alignment, now focused on policy advocacy for halting the race to superintelligence.
descriptions.macroscopic: Philanthropic foundation, Macroscopic Ventures, making grants and investments on global catastrophic risks, including AI safety and biosecurity.
descriptions.macrostrategy-research-initiative: Nick Bostrom's research initiative, founded after the Future of Humanity Institute closed, with no public website.
descriptions.manifund: Open platform for charitable funding, with regranting programs for AI safety and other causes, and the parent of Trace.
descriptions.mathematical-metaphysics-institute: Research institute searching for a mathematical basis for metaphysics and metaethics.
descriptions.mats-research: Fellowship program, ML Alignment & Theory Scholars, that pairs new researchers with established AI safety mentors for intensive research cohorts in Berkeley and London.
descriptions.metaculus: Online forecasting platform and aggregation engine, including AI progress and risk questions.
descriptions.model-evaluation-and-threat-research: Nonprofit, METR, that evaluates frontier AI models for dangerous autonomous capabilities and measures how fast those capabilities are growing.
descriptions.non-trivial: Program that helps high-school students start research in AI safety and biosecurity.
descriptions.nuclear-threat-initiative: Washington nonprofit working to reduce nuclear, biological and other catastrophic risks, including a biosecurity program on AI-enabled biological threats.
descriptions.openmined: Open-source nonprofit building privacy-preserving technology for analyzing non-public data, including for AI audits.
descriptions.orthogonal: AI alignment organization pursuing agent foundations research.
descriptions.oxford-martin-ai-governance-initiative: University of Oxford research program, AIGI, combining technical research on AI with policy analysis.
descriptions.palisade-research: AI safety research group building demonstrations of offensive AI capabilities and loss-of-control behaviors to inform policymakers.
descriptions.pauseai: Global grassroots movement campaigning for a pause on frontier AI development, through protests and lobbying, with national chapters.
descriptions.pauseai-us: US grassroots movement campaigning for a pause on frontier AI development.
descriptions.pour-demain: Swiss think tank working on resilience, including EU and Swiss policy on AI-enabled biological risks.
descriptions.principles-of-intelligence: Research organization, formerly PIBBSS, running fellowships and affiliate programs on the scientific foundations of AI alignment.
descriptions.rand-corporation: Nonpartisan research organization whose work includes AI policy and tools to assist policymakers.
descriptions.redwood-research: AI safety research nonprofit in Berkeley developing AI control techniques for keeping advanced models safe even if they are misaligned.
descriptions.rethink-priorities: Research organization producing analysis for effective altruist funders and organizations across animal welfare, global health, AI governance and existential risk.
descriptions.safe-ai-forum: Convenes the International Dialogues on AI Safety, bringing together senior scientists from the US, China and elsewhere on AI risk, and supports related research.
descriptions.saferai: French nonprofit building risk-management frameworks and ratings for AI developers, and advising on EU AI policy.
descriptions.sage: Nonprofit, Sage Future, that builds AI Digest explainers, the AI Village multi-agent demo, and forecasting tools such as Fatebook.
descriptions.schmidt-sciences: Philanthropic science funder founded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt, whose AI safety science program makes grants on technical safety research.
descriptions.secure-ai-project: Advocacy organization founded in 2024 that lobbies for state and federal laws requiring frontier AI developers to publish and follow safety and security protocols.
descriptions.securebio: Biosecurity nonprofit founded by Kevin Esvelt that builds pathogen early-warning systems, DNA synthesis screening and evaluations of AI biological risk.
descriptions.securedna: Swiss foundation providing free, privacy-preserving screening of DNA synthesis orders for hazardous sequences.
descriptions.sentinel: Forecasting team working to identify emerging global catastrophes early.
descriptions.sff: Grantmaking program, the Survival and Flourishing Fund, that distributes Jaan Tallinn's and other donors' money through rounds of volunteer recommenders.
descriptions.simon-institute-for-longterm-governance: Geneva think tank fostering international cooperation on governing transformative technologies, including AI.
descriptions.simplex: AI safety research organization working on mechanistic interpretability and a science of intelligence.
descriptions.speculative-technologies: Nonprofit industrial research lab running ambitious materials and manufacturing research programs that fit neither academia nor startups.
descriptions.stanford-existential-risks-initiative: Stanford University program hosting research, courses and fellowships on existential risks.
descriptions.stop-ai: Grassroots movement using non-violent direct action to disrupt the development of artificial general intelligence.
descriptions.taif: EA Funds' Transformative AI Fund, formerly the Long-Term Future Fund, which makes grants to individuals and small organizations working on AI safety.
descriptions.talos-network: Runs fellowships that place early-career people in AI policy organizations such as The Future Society and SaferAI.
descriptions.tarbell-center-for-ai-journalism: Runs fellowships and grants that place reporters in newsrooms to cover AI companies and AI policy.
descriptions.the-ai-policy-network: Advocacy organization, AIPN, lobbying for US federal policy on the path to AGI.
descriptions.the-ai-whistleblower-initiative: Independent nonprofit, AIWI, supporting insiders at frontier AI companies who want to raise safety concerns.
descriptions.the-bramble-center: Runs gatherings and workshops in the style of CFAR focused on practical courage and capability.
descriptions.the-future-society: Nonprofit think tank, TFS, in the US and Europe working on AI governance standards and policy.
descriptions.the-navigation-fund: Philanthropic foundation funded by Jed McCaleb making grants on AI safety, biosecurity, climate and other areas.
descriptions.timaeus: AI safety research organization applying singular learning theory to interpretability of neural networks.
descriptions.topos-institute: Research institute applying category theory and other mathematics to problems including AI alignment.
descriptions.transluce: Nonprofit research lab building open tools for understanding and overseeing AI systems.
descriptions.uk-aisi: The UK government's AI Security Institute, which tests frontier models and does research on AI safety and security.
descriptions.university-of-louisville-dr-roman-yampol: Roman Yampolskiy's research group at the University of Louisville, working on AI safety and security.
